title: Gangtok on a budget: real costs for 2026
meta_description: Gangtok on a budget in 2026: shared jeep and SNT bus fares, room rates, momo prices, Tsomgo seat costs and a daily budget from about ₹1,800 a person.
summary: A careful traveller can do Gangtok for about ₹1,800–2,500 a person a day in 2026: a shared jeep up from Siliguri for ₹350–550, a clean room for ₹1,500–2,500 split two ways, momos and thukpa for under ₹400 a day, and a shared Tsomgo seat instead of a reserved car. All prices are indicative.

sections.heading: What a budget day in Gangtok costs
paras: We sell trips from Gangtok every week, and the most common question we hear from students, young couples and families is simple: how little can this cost? The honest answer is that Gangtok is cheaper than most Himalayan hill towns once you are here, and more expensive than it needs to be if you arrive without a plan. The two things that blow a budget are reserved cars for every small hop and hotel rooms booked at the last minute in October or May.

The table below is what we see our own guests spend in 2026, per person, with two people sharing a room. It assumes you take shared transport where it exists, eat where people from Gangtok eat and do one permit day trip. Treat every figure as indicative: fares and room rates rise in the Durga Puja and Diwali weeks, over Christmas and in the May school holidays, and fall in the monsoon. Check current rates before you travel.

sections.heading: Getting up the hill for less
paras: Most budget travellers reach Gangtok from New Jalpaiguri station (NJP), Siliguri or Bagdogra airport. The road is NH10, about 115–125 km and 4–5.5 hours up the Teesta valley through Sevoke, Melli and the Rangpo check post. NH10 closes after landslides in the monsoon, usually June to September; the alternative is the longer road via Kalimpong and Lava or Algarah, which adds two to four hours. Check current road status before you travel.

Your three cheap options are the shared jeep, the SNT bus and a shared cab booked through your hotel. Shared jeeps (Sumos and Boleros, about ten seats) leave Siliguri and NJP when full and drop you at the Deorali area of Gangtok for about ₹350–550 a seat. Sikkim Nationalised Transport, the state bus service that began in 1944 as Sikkim State Transport under the kingdom, runs Siliguri–Gangtok buses through the day from about ₹250 for an ordinary seat to about ₹500 for an AC coach. The bus is slower but the safest cheap ride, and the ticket counter is next to the Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus in Siliguri.

A reserved small car from NJP or Bagdogra costs about ₹3,000–3,500, which is good value for a group of three or four with luggage. Avoid the touts inside the airport hall who quote double; the prepaid and syndicate counters outside are fairer.
list: Shared jeep NJP or Siliguri to Gangtok: about ₹350–550 a seat, 4.5–5.5 h
SNT bus Siliguri to Gangtok: about ₹250–500, 5–6 h
Reserved small car NJP or Bagdogra to Gangtok: about ₹3,000–3,500 a vehicle
Buy two seats if you have a big rucksack: it costs less than a sore back

sections.heading: Cheap and clean rooms
paras: Budget rooms in Gangtok cost ₹1,500–3,000 a night for a double in 2026, and the best value sits in the lanes behind MG Marg, along Tibet Road and in Development Area. Hostel beds start at about ₹500. Pay a little more for a room within a 10-minute walk of MG Marg: you will not need a taxi in the evening, and a single reserved hop across town costs ₹150–300.

Ask three questions before you book. First, is there heating? From November to February night temperatures in Gangtok fall to about 4–5 °C, and many cheap rooms charge extra for a heater. Second, how many steps from the road? Gangtok is built on a ridge, and some cheap hotels are 100 steps below the car. Third, is the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee included? Since 14 March 2025 hotels collect ₹50 per person at check-in as the state's Tourism Sustainable Development fee, valid for 30 days, with children under 5 exempt. You pay it once per trip, so keep the receipt.

sections.heading: Eating well for ₹400 a day
paras: Gangtok's cheapest food is also its best. A plate of steamed momos (usually eight to ten pieces) costs about ₹80–150 in a small eatery, a bowl of thukpa ₹100–180, and a full vegetarian thali with rice, dal, a seasonal sabzi and achar ₹150–250. Tea is ₹20–30 a cup. The small places on the lanes off MG Marg, in Lal Market and around the SNT bus stand serve office workers and drivers, which is the best guarantee of fresh food at fair prices.

Cafés on MG Marg charge Kolkata prices: ₹250–450 for a coffee and a cake. Enjoy one, then eat lunch where the taxi drivers eat. Bottled water is the hidden cost. Carry a refillable bottle and fill it from your hotel's filtered water; parts of Sikkim restrict packaged water bottles at times, and you save ₹60–100 a day.
list: Thukpa or thenthuk: about ₹100–180 a bowl
Sel roti and tea at a stall: about ₹40–60
Café coffee on MG Marg: about ₹150–250

sections.heading: Sightseeing without a reserved car
paras: Gangtok's taxis are run by syndicates. There are no meters; fares are fixed by route and by vehicle type, and you book from a stand, a hotel or an agent. The famous 3-point, 7-point and 10-point city tours are reserved-car products: in our 2026 experience a half-day 7-point tour in a small car costs about ₹2,500–3,500 and a full day about ₹4,000–4,500 for the vehicle. Split four ways that is fair. For two people, much of the town can be done on foot and by shared local taxi.

Walk MG Marg, Lal Market, the Do Drul Chorten and the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology area, which are all within about 2 km along the ridge and downhill. The Gangtok ropeway, about 1 km with three stations from Deorali to Tashiling, is a short paid ride with good town views. Shared local taxis run fixed routes, and shared jeeps to Rumtek cost about ₹100–150 a seat. Save your reserved car for Hanuman Tok and Tashi View Point at dawn, where no shared transport goes early enough.

For Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir, ask your hotel or a registered agent for a shared seat. The permit is arranged by the agent the day before with a photo ID and two passport photos, and Nathu La is for Indian nationals only, usually closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. A shared seat to Tsomgo and Baba Mandir costs about ₹1,000–1,300 including the permit in 2026, and with Nathu La about ₹1,300–1,600. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Where budgets leak and how to stop it
paras: Most overspending in Gangtok is avoidable. Book rooms for October, late December and May 6–8 weeks ahead, because last-minute rates near MG Marg can run 30–40 percent higher. Never accept a hotel-lobby quote for Tsomgo without comparing one registered agent; the difference can be ₹1,000 a vehicle. Do not hire a car for North Sikkim on the day: the permit has to be applied for through a registered agent and vehicle, operators require a minimum 2-night stay, and a cobbled-together trip costs more than a shared-seat package, which in 2026 runs about ₹6,500–9,000 a person for 2 nights in Lachung with meals.

Finally, keep a small buffer. Landslides close roads, permits get held for snow at Nathu La, and the cheapest way to absorb a lost day is an extra night in a budget room, not a rushed reserved car. If you want us to put a trip together for you, our Gangtok budget journeys start at the shared-transport level and tell you exactly what each part costs.

faqs.q: How much does a 3-day Gangtok trip cost on a budget?
faqs.a: About ₹7,000–10,000 per person for 3 nights in 2026, sharing a room, using shared jeeps from Siliguri or NJP and one shared Tsomgo seat. That covers a ₹1,500–2,500 room, simple meals, local transport and the ₹50 state tourist fee. Reserved cars for every sightseeing day push it towards ₹12,000–14,000. Prices are indicative; check current rates before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to reach Gangtok from NJP?
faqs.a: The SNT bus from Siliguri is the cheapest, at about ₹250 for an ordinary seat, followed by a shared jeep from NJP or Siliguri at about ₹350–550 a seat. Both take 4.5–6 hours on NH10. NH10 closes after monsoon landslides, when traffic goes via Kalimpong and Lava, adding 2–4 hours. Check current road status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there a cheap hotel near MG Marg in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes. The lanes behind MG Marg, Tibet Road and Development Area have clean rooms at about ₹1,500–3,000 a night for two in 2026, and hostel beds start near ₹500. Ask about heating from November to February, the number of steps from the road and whether the ₹50 state tourist fee is on the bill. Book 6–8 weeks ahead for October and May.

faqs.q: Can I visit Tsomgo Lake without booking a full car?
faqs.a: Yes. Registered agents and many hotels sell shared seats in Tsomgo vehicles, about ₹1,000–1,300 a person in 2026 including the permit. You hand over a photo ID and two passport photos the day before. Foreigners can visit Tsomgo too but need a group of two or more through an agent. Check current permit rules before you travel.

faqs.q: How much is a plate of momos in Gangtok?
faqs.a: About ₹80–150 for a plate of eight to ten steamed momos in a small local eatery in 2026, and more on MG Marg cafés. Fried and kothey momos cost a little extra. Pork, chicken and vegetable versions are common everywhere; beef momos are served in some Tibetan-run places. A filling local lunch of momos and soup is usually under ₹250.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay an entry fee to enter Sikkim?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 14 March 2025 Sikkim charges a ₹50 per tourist Tourism Sustainable Development fee, collected by your first hotel at check-in. It is valid for 30 days, so later hotels should not charge it again, and children under 5 are exempt. Keep the receipt. Check current status before you travel, as state fees can change.

No. Gangtok taxis run under syndicates with fixed fares by route and vehicle type, and there are no meters. Short reserved hops across town cost about ₹150–300 in 2026, and shared local taxis on fixed routes are far cheaper. Always confirm the fare before you get in, and book sightseeing cars through your hotel or a registered agent.

faqs.q: When is Gangtok cheapest to visit?
faqs.a: The monsoon months, roughly mid-June to mid-September, and late January to February are the cheapest, with hotel discounts of 20–40 percent off peak rates. The trade-off is landslide risk on NH10 in the monsoon and cold nights with possible snow closures at Nathu La in winter. March and late November offer a good balance of price and weather.

faqs.q: Is a budget North Sikkim trip possible from Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes. A shared-seat package to Lachung and Yumthang for 2 nights, with permit, simple lodge and meals, costs about ₹6,500–9,000 a person in 2026. Permits are issued only through Sikkim Tourism-registered agents and vehicles, operators require a minimum 2-night stay and children under 5 are not permitted. Check current road and permit status before you travel.
